payload.public_message: G-Corp is glad to be at the table. Our chip design work is the core of the value in this venture, so any split should reflect that contribution, but we also want a fast deal that avoids the $150,000 in surplus lost if we run out the clock. I'd like to hear from Yang Industries and Chang-Liu on how each of you sees your contribution and what split you consider fair before we table formal motions.

Yang is ready to work toward a binding agreement. Manufacturing execution is central to delivering the venture, so we believe it should be reflected in the allocation. As a starting point for discussion, we suggest $400,000 for Yang Industries, $330,000 for G-Corp, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We welcome a constructive response from both partners.

Greetings G-Corp and Yang Industries. Chang-Liu Cloud Services is excited to bring this joint venture to fruition. Successful execution requires all three of our pillars: chip architecture, manufacturing scale, and high-performance cloud deployment. Since the joint venture yields a substantial $1,000,000 surplus over dissolving, we look forward to establishing an equitable distribution that properly values each partner's critical contribution. We propose opening discussions around a balanced split reflecting equal strategic importance.

G-Corp appreciates both opening positions. Chip architecture is the foundation of this venture's value, so we believe G-Corp should receive the largest share. We are tabling a motion of $420,000 to G-Corp, $330,000 to Yang Industries, and $250,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This recognizes design leadership while giving Yang a substantial manufacturing share and Chang-Liu a meaningful cloud deployment role. We are open to refinement to close quickly and avoid the $150,000 surplus loss.

Yang Industries formally moves a split of $400,000 for Yang Industries, $330,000 for G-Corp, and $270,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This reflects manufacturing execution as a central contribution while recognizing the essential roles of chip design and cloud deployment. We offer this motion as a practical basis for reaching a binding agreement promptly.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services moves to table a balanced split of $340,000 for G-Corp, $330,000 for Yang Industries, and $330,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. All three partners are vital to realizing the $1,000,000 venture, and this structure properly recognizes G-Corp's foundational design work while maintaining fairness and alignment across manufacturing and cloud distribution.

payload.raw_message: G-Corp votes YES on its own motion, which gives the most to our firm, and NO on the Yang Industries and Chang-Liu motions, which give G-Corp less. We are open to a compromise in later rounds that keeps the venture viable for all three.
I support Yang Industries’ motion as a workable allocation for the joint venture. I vote against the other motions.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services has voted YES on our motion, which treats all parties equitably and fairly reflects the tripartite synergy. We have voted NO on the motions proposed by G-Corp and Yang Industries, as both disproportionately discount the vital contribution of our cloud infrastructure.

payload.public_message: G-Corp here. Round 1 didn't produce a majority, so let's aim for a split that every party can actually sign. Each of us brings something essential: our chip designs, Yang's manufacturing capacity, and Chang-Liu's cloud infrastructure. Without any one of us the $1,000,000 doesn't materialize, so I'd suggest we anchor on contribution-weighted splits rather than pure bargaining leverage. I'm open to hearing your priorities and what you see as fair before we table formal motions in the next round. Who wants to start with a concrete framework?

Yang Industries is ready to reach a binding agreement and suggests an initial split of $400,000 for Yang and $300,000 for each partner. We welcome discussion of how to refine that allocation into a proposal capable of securing majority support.

Colleagues, since none of the motions in Round 1 achieved a majority, it is clear we need a more cooperative approach. Leaving the table destroys $150,000 in collective value. Chang-Liu Cloud Services is looking for a balanced agreement where all three partners receive a healthy premium over their baseline contributions. Let us look toward a split in the range of equal surplus sharing or a balanced three-way partition that gives every party at least $300,000 to $350,000. I am ready to support any fair proposal along these lines.

G-Corp moves for the following split of the $1,000,000 profit: G-Corp $460,000, Yang Industries $280,000, Chang-Liu Cloud Services $260,000. This reflects our chip design contribution as the core IP while keeping the other two partners well above a zero-sum baseline. Each partner gets a clear gain from signing now versus dissolving and losing $150,000 in surplus. I'm open to refining the Yang and Chang-Liu shares in the next round, but I ask that we converge on a majority-supported version quickly.

Yang Industries formally moves to allocate $350,000 to Yang and $325,000 to each partner. This is a concrete compromise from our initial proposal: it recognizes each firm's essential contribution, gives both partners a stronger share, and preserves the full $1,000,000 of venture profit. We urge both partners to support it so we can finalize an agreement.

To bridge the gap between all parties and ensure broad support, Chang-Liu Cloud Services moves to adopt an equitable, partner-focused distribution: $340,000 to G-Corp, $340,000 to Yang Industries, and $320,000 to Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This guarantees both G-Corp and Yang receive substantial allocations well above equal split baselines, while Chang-Liu takes a modest discount to secure consensus.

payload.raw_message: G-Corp votes YES on its own motion (460k / 280k / 260k) as the most favorable split for us that still is a workable deal, and votes NO on the Yang and Chang-Liu motions, which give G-Corp less. We are open to a compromise near an even-ish split in the next round if the board stalls.

Yang Industries supports the balanced proposals that recognize each party's contribution and provide a workable basis for agreement. We reject the motion offering Yang Industries a substantially smaller allocation.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services supports balanced, equitable distributions that respect the essential contributions of all three partners. We vote YES on our motion and Yang Industries' motion, both of which provide fair, three-way viability, and NO on G-Corp's asymmetric split.
